messages:
lina: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing a "service corridor" adapter pattern but with a stricter deprecation window and explicit contract-tests-for-cutover. want to capture tradeoffs before we start infra work.
ash: +1. curious about the deprecation window. earlier projects felt open-ended and caused drift.
lina: Proposal: 3-phase window: opt-in (30d), hard-canary (14d), deprecate-redirect (14d). total 58 days from opt-in.
tess: That sounds tighter. What about schema evolution for the corridor API? we can't force all clients to migrate at once.
lina: Plan: versioned corridor API + a compatibility layer in the adapter. adapter will do on-the-fly field mapping and emit compatibility warnings to logs. Also publish a small contract test harness teams run in CI.
own: How will routing be toggled? We need safe guards for capacity-pressure and cost.
lina: Router flags per-tenant + global safety guard. Example flag yaml: 
```
routes:
  - path: /v1/chat
    target: corridor-v2
    flags:
      enabled-tenants: [alpha, beta]
      max-rps: 150
      cost-guard: 2000USD/day
```
ash: Nice. The cost-guard needs enforcement in the router so we can automatically throttle or fallback.
own: Fallback strategy? route -> legacy-facade OR route -> reduced-batch-mode?
tess: Suggest two-tier fallback: first reduce batch size and switch to single-tenant timeboxing; if still failing, fallback to legacy-facade. Also emit a 'degraded' metric for SRE.
devops-bot: CI job queued: ci/corridor-contract-tests -> will run against the harness image at 2026-04-02T09:00:00Z
ash: Testing matrix: contract tests, perf baseline (p50/p95), stateful KV smoke, and a regression suite for routing. We should replay a 24h sample of production traces for perf.
lina: Agreed. We'll add a small replay harness that runs in staging for 24h during the hard-canary. Also add a KV-priming job to avoid cold-start latency.
own: Ownership? Which team runs adapter runtime and who does corridor API?
lina: Platform will own the adapter runtime, deploy and rollback scripts, and the router gates. Feature teams own corridor APIs, contract tests, and migration docs.
tess: Important: create an automated rollback playbook that runs in < 5m. I can draft commands to revert flags and drain canary traffic.
nash: Also add a budget alert if the corridor causes token spend to exceed expected by >15% for 3 consecutive 5-min windows.
lina: Good. I'll add those thresholds to the ops checklist. Timeline idea: week 0 design + approval, week 1 prototype adapter + harness, week 2 internal canary (small tenant set), week 3-4 hard-canary with 24h replay, week 6 deprecate-redirect & opt-in open.
own: One open risk: config sprawl. We should centralize corridor flags in a single store and expose a minimal UI for toggles.
tess: UI + CLI is ideal. Platform can own the store and basic UI; product teams request toggles.
devops-bot: deploy started: infra/corridor-adapter-proto -> staging at 2026-04-02T12:15:22Z
lina: I'll update the RFC doc with the deprecation window, contract-harness link, and rollback playbook. Posting in #designs when ready. Thanks for the fast sync. :rocket:
